items.description: Delete abandoned SvelteKit/Tauri residue that contradicts ADR-0002 and is not referenced by live source.
steps: Confirm no live source imports or package scripts reference `packages/desktop-core`, `packages/desktop-protocol`, or `packages/sidecar` as abandoned-port modules.
Remove stale abandoned-port generated artifacts and any workspace metadata that would make them appear as active modules.
Preserve the Electron Desktop App and live packages only; do not reintroduce Sidecar, Desktop Protocol, or platform adapters.
Run the required verification gates and record the deletion-test result in progress.
items.regression_notes: Removed abandoned SvelteKit/Tauri package/app workspace residue. `pnpm install --lockfile-only` removed stale `apps/svelte-desktop`, `packages/desktop-core`, `packages/desktop-protocol`, `packages/sidecar`, and `@pi-gui/desktop-core` Electron lockfile entries; deleted tracked `apps/svelte-desktop/.gitignore` and ignored generated residue directories. Deletion test found no abandoned package/app dirs or workspace references in package.json, apps, packages, or pnpm-lock.yaml. Required gates passed: pnpm typecheck; pnpm --filter @pi-gui/desktop test:unit.

items.description: Replace the `pi-sdk-driver` ambient session-driver type copy with the real `@pi-gui/session-driver` package type Interface.
steps: Remove or neutralize `packages/pi-sdk-driver/src/vendor/session-driver.d.ts` so it no longer shadows the real package contract.
Adjust `packages/pi-sdk-driver` TypeScript configuration or project build order so imports from `@pi-gui/session-driver` and `@pi-gui/session-driver/runtime-types` resolve to the real package types.
Fix any resulting compile errors by updating the true source types or consumers, not by creating a second copied contract.
Run focused package builds for `session-driver` and `pi-sdk-driver` plus the required verification gates.
items.regression_notes: Removed `packages/pi-sdk-driver/src/vendor/session-driver.d.ts` so `pi-sdk-driver` no longer shadows the real `@pi-gui/session-driver` and `@pi-gui/session-driver/runtime-types` contracts. Existing package build order already builds `session-driver` before `pi-sdk-driver`, so the real package type Interface resolved through workspace exports without TypeScript config changes. Focused builds passed: `pnpm --filter @pi-gui/session-driver build`; `pnpm --filter @pi-gui/pi-sdk-driver build`. Required gates passed: `pnpm typecheck`; `pnpm --filter @pi-gui/desktop test:unit`.

items.description: Deepen the Desktop App state transition module for composer and selected-session state invariants.
steps: Extend `apps/desktop/electron/app-state-reducer.ts` or an adjacent state transition module to own composer draft, attachment, selected-session, revision, and error-clearing invariants for one coherent slice.

Update `app-store-composer.ts`, `app-store-workspace.ts`, or `app-store.ts` callers in that slice to use the deeper state transition Interface instead of hand-mutating the same `DesktopAppState` fields.
Keep side effects such as driver calls, persistence, and transcript publication outside the pure transition Implementation unless the selected design explicitly documents a safe internal seam.
Add unit tests at the state transition Interface proving no-op behavior, revision/error conventions, and selected-session/composer consistency.
Run the required verification gates and any focused tests for the touched state slice.
items.regression_notes: Extended `apps/desktop/electron/app-state-reducer.ts` so the Desktop App state transition Module owns composer draft sync, composer attachment replacement, and selected-session/composer consistency invariants. Updated composer and selected-session callers to use the reducer Seam while keeping driver calls, persistence, transcript publication, and other side-effect Implementations outside it. Added reducer Interface tests for no-op identity, revision/lastError conventions, attachment equality, and selection-to-threads composer state consistency. Focused and required gates passed: `pnpm --filter @pi-gui/desktop test:unit -- app-state-reducer`; `pnpm typecheck`; `pnpm --filter @pi-gui/desktop test:unit`.

items.description: Add a Desktop App IPC command registry or contract test that prevents drift between channel names, preload methods, renderer types, and main handlers.
steps: Introduce a small owning module for Desktop App IPC command metadata, or a contract test over the existing metadata, without broadening the renderer's Node access.
Prove every exposed `window.piApp` command has a known channel and every command channel expected by the renderer has a main-process handler or documented event-only role.
Keep listener/event channels such as state changes, selected transcript changes, terminal output, and theme changes explicit so they are not confused with request/response commands.
Update preload, main, or IPC types only as needed for the selected seam; avoid product UI changes.
Run the required verification gates and the new IPC contract test.

items.description: Create one owning Desktop App timeline model module for persisted transcript rows and live session events.
steps: Introduce a timeline model module that owns assembly of product-visible timeline rows from persisted transcript messages and live `SessionDriverEvent` inputs.
Move or wrap existing behavior from `app-store-timeline.ts`, `timeline-types.ts`, and `timeline-grouping.ts` behind a smaller Interface while preserving current rendering output.
Cover assistant deltas, queued user messages, tool lifecycle rows, run summaries, meta activity extraction, and reopened transcript behavior with tests at the timeline model Interface.
Update Desktop App callers to use the owning timeline model module without changing visible conversation-first behavior.
Run the required verification gates and focused timeline tests.

items.description: Deepen one internal `SessionSupervisor` concern while preserving the external `PiSdkDriver` Interface.
steps: Choose one high-friction concern inside `packages/pi-sdk-driver/src/session-supervisor.ts`, such as queued message delivery, extension host UI state, runtime command compatibility, or workspace/session catalog sync.
Extract that concern into an internal module with a smaller Interface and keep `PiSdkDriver` and `SessionDriver` caller behavior unchanged.
Use a real internal seam only where behavior varies or tests need locality; do not introduce pass-through Adapters for their own sake.
Add or update tests that exercise the extracted concern through its Interface and through the public driver path where practical.
Run focused `pi-sdk-driver` tests or builds plus the required verification gates.
